extracted.intended_audience: graduate students and researchers in mathematical physics / representation theory (string theory, BRST quantization, infinite-dimensional Lie algebras)
extracted.subtask_short: semi-infinite cohomology of graded lie algebras
extracted.subtask_description: Definitions, constructions and theorems for the semi-infinite cohomology complex of graded Lie (and super-Lie) algebras, and applications to BRST cohomology in string theory (Virasoro and NSR algebras), including vanishing theorems and the no-ghost theorem. Covers module categories, filtrations, spectral-sequence arguments, and hermitian/duality conditions needed for proofs.

rubrics_metrics.name: graded Lie algebra of finite growth
rubrics_metrics.description: g = ⊕_{n∈Z} g_n is a graded complex Lie algebra of finite growth: g_m, g_n ⊂ g_{m+n} and dim g_m < ∞.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This finiteness hypothesis is required so sums appearing in constructions (normal ordering, action on semi-infinite forms) are finite; it underpins many subsequent definitions (restricted dual, degree formulas, renormalizations).

rubrics_metrics.name: restricted dual g'
rubrics_metrics.description: g' denotes the restricted dual consisting only of finite linear combinations of elements of the graded dual (the 'restricted dual' is much smaller than the full dual).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the restricted dual to form the space of semi-infinite forms; this ensures graded/finite combinatorics and makes interior/exterior operators well-defined.

rubrics_metrics.name: semi-infinite form (semi-infinite condition)
rubrics_metrics.description: The space Λ^{∞}g' is spanned by monomials ω = e'_{i1} ∧ e'_{i2} ∧ ··· with i1 > i2 > ··· and the property that for large enough k one has i_{k+1} = i_k − 1 (equivalently only a finite number of basis elements of g'^{-} are missing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This 'finite number of holes in the Dirac sea' condition characterizes allowed monomials and is the algebraic incarnation of the ghost Fockspace; constructions and degree counts rely on this property.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clifford module structure via interior/exterior products
rubrics_metrics.description: Define operators ι(x) and ε(x') acting on Λ^{∞}g' by interior and exterior products with relations [ι(x), ε(y')] = ⟨x,y'⟩, ι(x)ι(y)=0, ε(x')ε(y')=0, yielding a representation of the Clifford algebra Cl(g ⊕ g').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These operators realize the ghost algebra; check the stated anticommutation relations and use normal ordering when infinite sums occur.

rubrics_metrics.name: projective vs honest representation and central extension condition
rubrics_metrics.description: Semi-infinite forms typically afford only a projective representation ρ of g; one has [ρ(x),ρ(y)] = ρ([x,y]) + γ(x,y) where γ = λ + dβ. The class of λ in H^2(g) determines whether ρ can be turned into an honest representation by choosing β; uniqueness of β holds iff H^1(g)=0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To obtain an honest representation you may need to pass to the universal central extension of g (adjoin generators to kill H^2), or tensor the semi-infinite forms with a module M whose projective class cancels γ.

rubrics_metrics.name: degree / ghost-number grading
rubrics_metrics.description: Assign Deg ω0 ∈ Z, Deg ε(x') = +1, Deg ι(x) = −1 and extend to Λ^{∞} to define a Deg (ghost number) grading on Λ^{∞} and on complexes C^{∞}(g;M).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This grading (ghost number) is preserved by the representation ρ and is crucial to define the bigrading used in spectral sequences and to track cohomological degrees.

rubrics_metrics.name: module category O hypotheses
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider graded g-modules M in category O: graded modules with dim M_n < ∞ and there exists n0 such that M_n = 0 for n > n0 (subcategory O_0 when appropriate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Category O conditions ensure formal characters are well-defined and that sums in the differential are finite; closure under tensor products allows constructing complexes M ⊗ Λ^{∞} staying in O.

rubrics_metrics.name: differential d on M ⊗ Λ^{∞} and nilpotency condition
rubrics_metrics.description: Define d ≡ Σ_i π(e_i) ε(e'_i) + Σ_{i<j} : ι([e_i,e_j]) ε(e'_i) ε(e'_j) : + ε(β) on M ⊗ Λ^{∞} (formula VI.1.20). The key property is that d^2 = 0, which depends on M ⊗ Λ^{∞} being a g-module and on finiteness from M ∈ O.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify nilpotency d^2=0 via direct (tedious) calculation; ensure finite-growth and category O hypotheses so sums are finite.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hermitian modules and duality theorem
rubrics_metrics.description: If g admits an antilinear involution σ with σ(g_n) = g_{−n} and M is a Hermitian module with π(x)† = −π(σ(x)), then one can define a non-degenerate Hermitian form on C^{∞}(g;M) with d† = d, yielding a duality H^m(g;M) ≅ H^{−m}(g;M).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose the normalization of the inner product as in the text; this self-adjointness allows use of Hodge-type arguments and propagates vanishing via duality.

rubrics_metrics.name: relative semi-infinite subcomplex and compatibility with central elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Define C^{∞}(g,h;M) = { ω ∈ C^{∞}(g;M) | ι(x)ω = θ(x)ω = 0 ∀ x ∈ h } whose cohomology H^{∞}(g,h;M) is stable under d. If h contains the center z and z acts by scalars on M, then θ(z)ω = 0 forces π(z) = −⟨β,z⟩·1_M; thus π must be a projective representation of the opposite class for any non-trivial relative cohomology to exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This compatibility condition fixes critical parameters in string-theoretic applications (e.g. central charge / critical dimension).

rubrics_metrics.name: vanishing theorem criterion: freeness over n^-
rubrics_metrics.description: Fundamental theorem: if M is a free n^{-}-module (e.g. M ≅ U(n^{-}) of rank one), then the relative cohomology H^m(g,g_0;M) is concentrated at zero degree (vanishes for m ≠ 0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the central algebraic input for BRST/no-ghost theorems: freeness over the negative subalgebra implies vanishing of semi-infinite cohomology outside degree zero.

rubrics_metrics.name: construction of bounded filtration and spectral-sequence convergence
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduce a filtration fdeg (e.g. fdeg(m⊗ω) = deg_m − deg_ω^+ + deg_ω^−) and verify that all homogeneous pieces of d have non-negative filtration degree so (F^p C, d) is a bounded filtered complex; Theorem II.1.32 then gives a spectral sequence converging finitely to the cohomology whose E1 term is cohomology of the associated graded complex with induced differential d0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute filtration degrees of each oscillator/term (tables provided) to check the non-negativity condition; identify the fdeg=0 part to read off d0.

rubrics_metrics.name: E1-term identification via Künneth and g0-invariants
rubrics_metrics.description: The E1-term of the spectral sequence (after the chosen filtration) is E^{c,b}_1 = * H^c(n_+) ⊗ H^b_{∞}(n^-;M)^{g_0}, where g_0-invariants are taken and the Künneth formula is applied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute H^b_{∞}(n^-;M) (see Appendix theorem); if g_0 acts reducibly on K then H(K^{g_0}) = H(K)^{g_0}, simplifying computations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix result: semi-infinite cohomology of n^- with free coefficients
rubrics_metrics.description: For M ≅ U(n^{-}) (a free n^{-}-module) one has H^b_{∞}(n^-;M) ≅ ℂ for b = 0 and 0 otherwise (Theorem VI.A.1 / VI.A.2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is proved by filtering the complex, passing to the associated graded, and constructing an explicit chain homotopy Γ showing triviality except in degree zero; use this in spectral-sequence E1 computations to deduce vanishing.

rubrics_metrics.name: identification of semi-infinite forms for Virasoro with ghost Fock space
rubrics_metrics.description: For the Virasoro algebra V, Λ^{∞}V' can be identified with the ghost Fockspace by b_n ↔ ι(L_n) and c_n ↔ ε(L'_{−n}); choose an sl(2,C)-invariant vacuum ω0 = 6'1 ∧ 6'0 ∧ 6'_{−1} ∧ ···.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This identification yields the standard ghost anticommutation rules and matches the Degree with ghost number; allows translation of algebraic cohomology statements into the BRST/ghost language.

rubrics_metrics.name: BRST operator / differential for open bosonic string
rubrics_metrics.description: The differential is expressed via conformal fields as d = ∮_{C_0} dz j(z) with j(z) = : (T_M + 1/2 T_{gh}) c : (equations VI.2.10–VI.2.11).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specialize π(c) = 26·1_M and work in the subcomplex relative to the center to realize the BRST complex of the open bosonic string; the field expressions make calculations and spectral-sequence filtrations explicit.

rubrics_metrics.name: freeness of string Fock module M(k) for nonzero momentum
rubrics_metrics.description: Brower proved that for k ≠ 0 the Fock module M(k) is a free V^{-}-module (i.e., obtained by action of negative Virasoro modes on the vacuum), hence the hypotheses of the vanishing theorem are satisfied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Therefore for k ≠ 0 the relative BRST cohomology vanishes outside ghost number zero, a key step in proving the no-ghost theorem.

rubrics_metrics.name: signature vs character matching and positivity (No-Ghost Theorem)
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute generating functions for character ch_q and signature sgn_q of the complex (using an operator C implementing time-like sign flip and ghost conjugation). Equality of signature and character implies positivity of the inherited inner product on BRST cohomology and hence absence of negative-norm physical states (no-ghost theorem) for k ≠ 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define C so that C a^μ_n C = (−1)^δ_{μ0} a^μ_n and C acts as ghost conjugation on ghost modes; compute traces with C to obtain sgn_q and compare to ch_q.

rubrics_metrics.name: NSR string: vanishing theorem in Neveu–Schwarz sector
rubrics_metrics.description: For the Neveu–Schwarz super-Virasoro algebra N, define the relative subcomplex C^{∞}(N,V_0;M) with L_0 and b_0 invariance, introduce a half-integral filtration, get a spectral sequence whose E1-term is H(N_+) ⊗ H^{∞}(N^-;M)_{L_0}, and using appendix results H^{∞}(N^-;M) vanishes except in degree zero, hence H_m^{∞}(N,V_0;M) = 0 for m < 0 and, by duality, for m ≠ 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires decomposition into Verma modules, finiteness of the relative subcomplex, and existence (constructed in Appendix C) of a positive-definite inner product on cohomology to apply duality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ramond sector caveat: zero-mode complications and grading issues
rubrics_metrics.description: In the Ramond sector the presence of superconformal ghosts' zero modes makes the cochains infinitely degenerate and there is no unique treatment in the literature; two different treatments of zero modes produce isomorphic cohomologies but one fails to admit ghost-number grading, so the standard vanishing-by-ghost-number argument does not apply directly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Handle Ramond zero modes via carefully chosen filtrations and spectral-sequence manipulations; sometimes one must prove vanishing on an intermediate E-term and propagate it through successive spectral sequences. Expect only finite (two-fold) degeneracy in final cohomology.
